purpose: Clean low-poly camp and ship models for the 3D campaign map (진영 전역): joseon, japan and ming camps at tiers 1-3 and one map ship per navy.

images.shipStyle: A single isolated 3D game-asset render made for image-to-3D conversion. One sixteenth-century East Asian wooden warship modelled as a single object, shown whole from the keel to the top of the masts, standing on nothing. Camera: high three-quarter view about 35 degrees above the horizon, from the side and a little ahead of the ship, so the whole length of the hull, its deck and its sails are visible; the bow points to the lower left of the picture and the stern to the upper right; the whole model is centred and completely inside the frame with a generous empty margin all round. Lighting: soft, even, shadowless studio light from all sides, no cast shadows, no dark ambient-occlusion halos. Look: clean stylised realism like a premium historical strategy-game unit, chunky simplified shapes with thick masts and sails set full and bellied, large clearly readable forms and strong clean colours that still read when the ship is tiny on screen; no fine clutter, no rigging lines, no ropes, no oars, no anchors, no small props. Transparent background. No water, no sea, no waves, no wake, no stand or base, no other ships or boats, no people, no animals. Absolutely no text, letters, characters, numbers, logos, emblems or crests anywhere, no rising-sun flag, no sunburst, no watermark, no border.

ships.ship-joseon: Joseon Korean panokseon, 1592: a broad, flat two-level wooden hull with a square transom stern and a blunt square bow; the lower hull of dark brown timber, and above it a full-length upper deck enclosed all round by a high wall of plain light-brown wooden shield planks with small square gun ports; a small command pavilion with a grey tiled hip roof standing on the upper deck towards the stern; two masts carrying large square tan cloth sails; plain blue cloth banners at the mastheads and at the stern, with no emblem.
ships.ship-japan: Japanese atakebune, 1592: a long wooden hull of dark timber carrying a large box-like fortified superstructure along most of its length, its walls white plaster panels framed by black timber with small square gun ports, and on top of it towards the stern a small two-storey turret with black tiled roofs; one tall central mast carrying one large square sail of plain cream cloth; plain red and plain white nobori banners standing along the upper rail, with no emblem or symbol of any kind.
ships.ship-ming: Ming Chinese war junk, 1598: a sturdy wooden hull of red-lacquered timber with a flat transom bow and a high raised stern castle with red rails, two masts carrying tall battened junk sails of red-brown cloth stiffened by dark horizontal battens; plain yellow and plain red cloth banners at the mastheads and at the stern, with no emblem.

outcome.summary: Rejected by the owner: nothing from this package ships. public/models/camps keeps its earlier files and public/models/ships-map was never shipped.
outcome.camps: The whole-camp models stand on their own square ground slabs and read as toy dioramas, mushy close up. The camps are to be built from separate buildings on the terrain instead.
outcome.ships: Dropped for the battle's own ships: the campaign map now draws the procedural battle ships (src/ships/build) of the kinds each fleet has.

reviewBuild.note: Built locally for review only (scripts/build-map-models.mjs, not kept); none of these files ships.

convention.camp: glTF y up; waterfront (pier or quay) faces -z; lowest point on y = 0; centred on x and z; the longer horizontal side is 1 unit; near and far share one frame
convention.ship: glTF y up; bow towards +z; one unit long along z; centred on x and z; the waterline on y = 0 (the keel below it)

reviewBuild.method: Meshy Smart Topology meshes as made (turned, normalised, a camp slab's underside dropped, normals remade from the faces); far camp levels by meshoptimizer; the base colour filled outside its UV islands and downscaled to WebP
